turns.content: hey, i'm looking at our benefits handbook for the wellness premium credit thing and want to make sure i'm reading the deadlines right. so section 4.2 says the health risk assessment in the portal has to be done by october 31, but the biometric screening results can come in through december 1 via a physician attestation form. i've got my annual physical with dr. chen on november 14, which is after the october cutoff but way before december 1st. so that should still qualify for the credit, right? just want a sanity check before i put it all on the calendar.

Based on the wording you described, **yes—your November 14 physical appears to fit the screening deadline**, as long as you meet both requirements separately:

- **By October 31:** Complete the health risk assessment in the portal.
- **By December 1:** Make sure the biometric screening results are received through the physician attestation form.

The one thing to double-check is whether December 1 is only a **submission deadline**, with a separate deadline for when the screening itself must occur. I haven’t seen Section 4.2, so I can’t confirm that distinction from the handbook.

For your calendar, keep the October 31 assessment deadline and plan to have Dr. Chen complete the form at your November 14 visit, then submit it promptly. If you paste the relevant paragraph, I can check whether it specifies a separate screening-date cutoff.

yeah that sounds right, i think the assessment is just the questionnaire part that has to be done online by oct 31. the biometrics are separate. so my nov 14 physical would still work as long as dr. chen fills out whatever attestation form after. i'll put the assessment deadline on my calendar for like oct 20 so i don't forget. thanks for the sanity check

October 20 sounds like a good reminder for the questionnaire. Just keep the November 14 physical **tentative for credit eligibility** until you confirm there isn’t a separate screening-date cutoff—December 1 might only be the paperwork deadline.

Bring the attestation form to your visit, and aim to have it submitted and received before December 1 rather than leaving it until the last day.

hmm ok so i'm looking at section 4.3 now and it mentions "qualified biometric screening" but doesn't list specific panels or say whether standard fasting labs from a regular physical count. dr. chen usually orders the basic lipid panel and glucose. is that enough or do they want some special employer-specific form with extra stuff?

**A lipid panel and glucose might count, but “qualified biometric screening” alone doesn’t establish that.** Based on what you’ve shared, Section 4.3 doesn’t specify the required measurements or whether routine physical labs qualify.

Two separate things to check:
- **Required measurements:** Some programs also require blood pressure, height/weight, or waist circumference. Those are general examples—not confirmed requirements for your plan.
- **Required paperwork:** Your handbook’s reference to a “physician attestation form” suggests there’s a designated form Dr. Chen needs to complete, even if your usual labs are sufficient.

The best next step is to find that form in the wellness portal—it may list both the required measurements and the eligible screening dates. If it doesn’t, ask the wellness administrator:

> “Will a November 14 annual physical with a lipid panel and glucose qualify? What additional measurements, if any, are required, and which physician attestation form must be received by December 1?”

That should also settle the remaining date question before your appointment.

yeah fair point, i should probably just track down the actual attestation form in the portal to see what it asks for. dr. chen's office usually sends my labs to quest anyway so maybe they already have the right format. i'll check tomorrow

Yep—the portal’s attestation form is the best place to start. One small distinction: **Quest’s lab report may supply the results, but it isn’t necessarily a substitute for the employer’s required form.** Check the form for required measurements and screening dates, then send it to Dr. Chen’s office before your appointment so they know what’s needed.

hmm so section 4.5 mentions the credit applying starting january 1 payroll. does that mean if i get everything in by december 1 it kicks in jan 1 and i get the full $25 each month for the year? or is there some retroactive catch-up thing if paperwork lands late

**January 1 sounds like the scheduled start of the credit, but it doesn’t by itself establish a full year of payments or retroactive catch-up.** Based on the wording you’ve shared:

- **If you meet all requirements by their deadlines:** Section 4.5 appears to say the credit starts with January 1 payroll. If the stated amount is $25 per month, that would total **$300 over 12 months**, assuming you remain eligible throughout the year.
- **If paperwork arrives late:** We haven’t seen language saying whether late submissions are accepted, whether the credit starts later, or whether missed credits are paid retroactively. Don’t count on catch-up payments without an explicit provision.

Also, “January 1 payroll” could mean the first applicable paycheck in January rather than a payment issued on January 1.

Can you paste Section 4.5, including any language about late submissions or adjustments? That should let us distinguish what’s guaranteed from what still needs confirmation.
